size.note: Head and body 0.13-0.15 m, tail 0.10-0.13 m, mass 0.07-0.11 kg; a large, dark chipmunk with muted stripes. Built at 0.14 m head and body (nose to rump) and a 0.11 m tail held out behind; 0.057 m at the shoulder, 0.069 m at the top of the raised head; 0.246 m nose to tail tip in a straight line.

source.title: Townsend's chipmunk (variant of the California ground squirrel's Meshy mesh)
source.author: variant of otospermophilus_beecheyi by agent (Claude) for Aaron Brodeur
source.original: the California ground squirrel's text-to-3D preview, ai_model latest (meshy-7.1), triangle remesh to 20,000 faces (19,627 triangles, untextured)
source.prompt: (the ground squirrel's) A California ground squirrel (Otospermophilus beecheyi) walking on all four legs like a squirrel crossing a lawn: NOT sitting, NOT standing up, NOT a prairie dog, NOT a marmot, NOT a chipmunk. Single adult, side-on, body horizontal and long, back level, all four paws flat on the ground, front legs straight down under the shoulders, head held up and forward. Realistic proportions: head and body 26 cm, body a little heavier than a tree squirrel's but not fat, short legs, rounded head, small erect rounded ears, blunt muzzle, open dark eyes. Bushy flattened tail 18 cm long (two thirds of the body), wider than the hind leg, held straight out behind and level, not curled. Mottled grey-brown fur, pale grey shoulders, buff belly. No base, no ground. Game-ready, symmetric.

tiers.note: The back is cut along the stripe edges on lod0 and lod1 (the decimation is rescaled so the cut body meets its budget): lod0 = body + tail (10 sides x 12 rings, 240) + eyes (16); lod1 = body + tail (6 x 7, 84); lod2 = body (no stripe cuts: a dark median and muted bands) + tail (4 x 3, 24). GLB 166,580 bytes.

rig: Rodent template, exactly as client/assets/ground_squirrel.glb (tools/build_ground_squirrel.py, the sentinel sit-up) and to be loaded with its loader constants: BODY 0 (hindquarters), CHEST 7 (pivot at the lumbar: flexes with the bound, rises to sit up), HEAD 6 (pivot at the base of the neck) and LEG_A 1 (fore pair, elbows) children of the chest, LEG_B 2 (hind pair, stifles), TAIL 3 and TAIL_TIP 8 (child of the tail). extras.rig keys: kind, chest, tail, tail_tip, head, fore, hind, length_m. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a chipmunk from above and the side: five blackish-brown dorsal stripes separated by four pale ones (the inner pair grey-brown, the outer pair creamy), fading onto a grey-brown rump; tawny-orange sides; whitish belly; the striped face (dark through the eye and below it, cream between); ears dark in front, pale behind; a dark-centred tail edged buff-white and tawny below, held out behind. Built on the ground squirrel's body, slimmed 0.86x: still a little long-bodied and short-legged for a chipmunk, and the head is the ground squirrel's (blunt). Townsend's stripes are muted in life; these are crisp, read at game distance. lod2 (150 triangles) loses the hind legs into the body and shows only one fore leg from the side, and has no stripes (a dark median line). Eye on lod0 only, the cream ring painted on lod0 and lod1.

scientific_note: GBIF and the tile records file it as Tamias townsendii; many authors now place the western chipmunks in Neotamias (Neotamias townsendii).
